failure: CHK-002 – Output values while reset is asserted (7 fails, one per run, always @0 ps; sim.log:122, sim_runs/*.log)
spec_says: spec/uart_lite_Design_Specification.md:106 REQ-RST-002 "While i_rst_n is 0, the outputs shall have these values: o_txd = 1, o_tx_ready = 1, o_rx_valid = 0, o_rx_data = 0, o_rx_frame_err = 0, o_rx_overrun = 0." Line 104 REQ-RST-001: "When i_rst_n becomes 0, every flip-flop ... shall take its reset value at once". Line 358 ENV-002: "The environment shall hold i_rst_n at 0 for at least 2 cycles of i_clk at the start of a simulation." contract.json:705 (UL-12.1-02): "Applied as a stimulus constraint: every simulation starts with i_rst_n=0 for at least 2 i_clk cycles." The spec does not say what the outputs are at time 0, before any reset event has happened.
verification_does: Env.start() drives i_rst_n=1 at t=0 (verif/tests/test_uart_lite.py:144) and starts the clock (146). It waits two rising edges (149-152) and a falling edge (158). Only then does it call reset(), which waits another rising edge plus 0.3P and drives i_rst_n=0 (185-189), at about 46 ns. The SVA (verif/sva/nnc_chk_reset.sv:22-24) samples at every posedge with !i_rst_n. At the t=0 posedge the sampled i_rst_n is still the simulator default 0, because cocotb's write of 1 happens in the same time step. The sampled outputs are the un-reset 0 values, so o_txd===1 fails. The expected values come straight from REQ-RST-002. The failure is a time-0 initialisation and race artifact. nnc_tb_top.sv and nnc_cocotb.start_clock are not in this directory, so the exact clock phase at t=0 cannot be confirmed.
what_to_change: Fix test (recommended): in Env.start() (test_uart_lite.py:142-160), drive i_rst_n=0 before start_clock, so the outputs see a real reset before the first rising edge, and hold it for at least 2 cycles as ENV-002 and contract.json:705 require. Also make sure the clock's first rising edge comes after the reset is applied, for example by starting the clock low; that removes the t=0 race. Clarify spec (optional): add a sentence to REQ-RST-002/ENV-002 saying output values are only defined after the first assertion of i_rst_n has taken effect, so the checker has a defined start point. That matches the existing nnc_env.sv ENV-01 assumption.

failure: CHK-003 – Delivery into an empty holding register at V=M+2 (83 fails; first @318400000 ps = 318.4 us in test_chk_021_low_at_release)
spec_says: spec:172 REQ-RX-003 "While idle, the receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1) = 1 and s(T0) = 0." spec:222 REQ-FE-003 "After a frame with a frame error, the receiver shall not detect a new start bit until s has been 1 at one edge and 0 at the next edge ... so a line held at 0 produces exactly one frame." spec:321 REQ-ERR-001 and spec:326 REQ-ERR-003: a line that stays low gives exactly one 0x00 with o_rx_frame_err=1. D-005 (spec:412): "A 1-to-0 transition is required, so a break gives one byte." spec:200 REQ-RX-020 sets the load at V. The contract RX model (contract.json:781) says: "When idle, the start edge T0 is an edge with s(T0-1)=1 and s(T0)=0."
verification_does: Stimulus: test_chk_021 holds i_rxd=0 through reset release and for 40N cycles (test_uart_lite.py:961-967). test_chk_028(b) holds a 50N-cycle break with i_rx_ready=1 (1109-1112). test_chk_029/regression send frames with stop=0 followed by a gap of at least 1 (rx_random, 368-377). Expected value: the SVA reference model in verif/sva/nnc_chk_rx.sv:64-68 starts a frame whenever the model is idle and `!i_rxd`. It has no previous-sample term, so it does not check s(T0-1)=1. After a frame that ends with the line still low (break, or a stop=0 frame), it restarts at M+1 and produces phantom frames every H+9N+1 edges. The phantom V raises mdl_v (line 49), and CHK-003 (97-99) then expects a load that the spec forbids. Measured spacing of the fails: 3060 ns = 153 cycles = H+9N+1 for N=16 (318400, 321460, 324520, 327580 ns), and 780 ns = 39 cycles = 2+36+1 for N=4 (min.s1.log:125-128). That is exactly the restart period of the faulty model. The Python model in the same test uses `if self.prev_s == 1 and sv == 0` (test_uart_lite.py:321-323) and passes. test_chk_021 asserts "exactly one byte expected from the low line" (975-976), and test_chk_028(b) asserts exactly one delivery (1116-1119).
what_to_change: Fix the checker model (recommended; this makes it stricter, not weaker). In verif/sva/nnc_chk_rx.sv add `logic mdl_prev;`, set it to 1'b1 in the !i_rst_n branch (so s(R1-1)=1, REQ-RST-010), and update it with `mdl_prev <= i_rxd;` on every non-reset edge. Change the idle start condition at line 65 from `if (!i_rxd)` to `if (mdl_prev && !i_rxd)`. Then re-run all 7 configurations. CHK-003, CHK-005, CHK-006 and CHK-009 should all clear together, because they share this model.

failure: CHK-005 – Overrun drop at V keeps the held byte; one-cycle pulse (24 fails; first @993370000 ps = 993.37 us in test_chk_028_idle_break part (c); 0 fails in wide.s1)
spec_says: spec:226 REQ-OVR-001 drops the byte "At the delivery edge V of a completed frame, if o_rx_valid = 1 and i_rx_ready = 0". spec:228 REQ-OVR-002 gives a one-cycle o_rx_overrun pulse. spec:232 REQ-OVR-004: "o_rx_overrun shall be 0 in every cycle except the cycle after an edge at which a byte is dropped." Only a completed frame, started at a real T0 with s(T0-1)=1 and s(T0)=0 (spec:172 REQ-RX-003), has a V. spec:222 REQ-FE-003 / spec:321 REQ-ERR-001: "a line held at 0 produces exactly one frame" ("deliver the byte 0x00 ... or drop it with an overrun pulse").
verification_does: test_chk_028(c) (test_uart_lite.py:1122-1133): holds 0x77 with i_rx_ready=0, drives i_rxd=0 for long(50) cycles, then 1. It expects exactly one overrun pulse (1132) and 0x77 held (1133); this Python check passes. The SVA CHK-005 (verif/sva/nnc_chk_rx.sv:109-111) fires on every model V with o_rx_valid=1 && !i_rx_ready. The model (64-68) re-detects a 'start' on the still-low line at M+1 because it has no s(T0-1)=1 term, so it creates phantom V's every H+9N+1 cycles. Fails at 993370, 996430, 999490, 1002550 ns are 3060 ns = 153 cycles apart (N=16). In wide.s1 the low time is capped at 12N (test_uart_lite.py:132-133), so no phantom V happens before the line rises, and there are 0 fails.
what_to_change: Fix the checker model as for CHK-003: add a model previous-sample register in nnc_chk_rx.sv that resets to 1 and is updated with i_rxd each edge, and change the idle start condition to `mdl_prev && !i_rxd`. CHK-005 itself (lines 109-111) is correct once mdl_v is correct.

failure: CHK-006 – o_rx_overrun only after a drop edge (24 fails; first @993370000 ps, same timestamps as CHK-005; 0 fails in wide.s1)
spec_says: spec:232 REQ-OVR-004: "o_rx_overrun shall be 0 in every cycle except the cycle after an edge at which a byte is dropped." spec:226 REQ-OVR-001: a drop happens only "At the delivery edge V of a completed frame". spec:172 REQ-RX-003 (start needs s(T0-1)=1, s(T0)=0) and spec:222 REQ-FE-003 / D-005 (spec:412): a held-low line gives one frame. spec:236 REQ-OVR-006: glitches and reset-cut frames never pulse.
verification_does: The SVA (verif/sva/nnc_chk_rx.sv:85-94, 115-117) computes `drop_q <= mdl_v && o_rx_valid && !i_rx_ready` and asserts `o_rx_overrun == drop_q`. mdl_v comes from the faulty model at lines 64-68, which starts on any low sample while idle. On a line held low after the first frame it creates phantom drop edges every H+9N+1 cycles (993370, 996430, 999490, 1002550 ns; 153 cycles apart at N=16). Stimulus is test_chk_028(c), test_uart_lite.py:1122-1133. That test's own assertion of exactly one overrun pulse (1132) passes.
what_to_change: Fix the checker model (shared with CHK-003/005/009): add an s(E-1) register to the SVA RX model (reset to 1, updated to i_rxd each edge) and require `mdl_prev && !i_rxd` for a start. CHK-006 logic (lines 85-94, 115-117) needs no other change.

failure: CHK-009 – Empty register: data/flag stable unless a byte is loaded (80 fails; first @328460000 ps; fails come in pairs at one timestamp)
spec_says: spec:210 REQ-RX-025: "o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err shall change only at an edge where a new byte is loaded, or on reset." spec:212 REQ-RX-026: i_rx_ready has no effect while o_rx_valid=0. spec:200 REQ-RX-020: a load happens at V=M+2 of a completed frame. spec:180 REQ-RX-007 and spec:192 REQ-RX-013: a new start is detected at any edge with s(T0-1)=1, s(T0)=0 once the receiver is idle.
verification_does: The SVA (verif/sva/nnc_chk_rx.sv:133-141) has two properties, a_CHK_009 and a_CHK_009_b. Both increment fails_CHK_009 and print the same message, which explains the paired fails. Both assume no load unless the model has mdl_v/load_q. The faulty model (64-68) is busy with a phantom frame that started on a still-low line (no s(T0-1)=1 check), so it misses the real falling edge of the next frame. Timing confirms this. In chk_021, with R1 ≈ 312240 ns, phantom starts fall at R1+0/153/306/459/612. The phantom at R1+612 spans the real start of 0xA5 at R1+656, and the real V+1 = R1+811 → 328460 ns, the observed fail. In chk_029/regression, after a stop=0 frame with gap g=1, the phantom starts at M+1 and the real start is 8 cycles later; the observed CHK-003→CHK-009 delta is 160 ns = 8 cycles (2008120→2008280, base.s2 1387000→1387160). When a glitch follows the error frame the delta is 17 cycles (1976260→1976600, 2629040→2629380).
what_to_change: Fix the checker model (shared fix with CHK-003/005/006): add a model s(E-1) register (reset to 1) and start only on `mdl_prev && !i_rxd`. Optionally give a_CHK_009_b its own label or counter so the two sub-properties can be told apart in the log; this is diagnostic only and does not weaken either property.

failure: CHK-010 – Transmit handshake, acceptance condition and idle values (21 fails = 3 per run, always @0, @20000, @40000 ps)
spec_says: spec:140 REQ-TX-003 "While the transmitter is idle (no frame in progress), o_tx_ready shall be 1." spec:164 REQ-TX-014 "While the transmitter is idle, o_txd shall be 1." spec:358 ENV-002 "The environment shall hold i_rst_n at 0 for at least 2 cycles of i_clk at the start of a simulation." contract.json:705 says this is applied as a stimulus constraint. The idle state is only defined after reset (REQ-RST-009, spec:120); the spec says nothing about outputs before the first reset.
verification_does: Env.start() drives i_rst_n=1 at t=0 (test_uart_lite.py:144) and starts the clock (146). It then waits RisingEdge, RisingEdge, FallingEdge (149-158), and reset() waits another RisingEdge plus 0.3P before driving i_rst_n=0 (185-189). The SVA (verif/sva/nnc_chk_tx.sv:38-52, 62-65) has tx_pos=0 (2-state default) and is not disabled because i_rst_n=1. It expects idle values o_tx_ready=1 && o_txd=1 (part b), gets 0/0, and fails at exactly those three edges. The Python monitor does not see these edges: it is not armed until the first reset (test_uart_lite.py:251-259).
what_to_change: Fix test (recommended): in Env.start() (test_uart_lite.py:142-160), drive i_rst_n=0 before or at clock start and hold it for at least 2 cycles before the first release, as ENV-002 / contract.json:705 require. That removes the 3 CHK-010 fails and the CHK-002 @0 fail together. this does not weaken CHK-010. Clarify spec (optional): state that output values are defined only from the first reset assertion onward.
